title: Dense integer-lattice restriction for condensed ell-adic derived invariants
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $V$, put $V_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V)$ with the finite-dimensional product norm topology. For a topological group $J$, write $\mathcal A_F(J)$ for internal $C_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with an action of the condensed group $S\mapsto C(S,J)$; invariants are the equalizer imposing that action to be trivial, and $R\Gamma_J$ is their ordinary total right derived functor in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $r\geq0$, let $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ with its inverse-limit topology, and let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ with the discrete topology. The homomorphism $\iota:D\to L$ sends the $i$th standard integer basis vector to $1$ in the $i$th $\mathbf Z_\ell$ factor. Let $V$ have a continuous $E$-linear $L$-action. Restriction of actions along $\iota$ and the inclusion of invariant objects induce the canonical derived restriction morphism
$$b_F:R\Gamma_L(V_F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota V_F).$$
This is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. Its degree-zero map is the identity after identifying $L$-invariants and $D$-invariants. The morphism is natural in continuous equivariant $E$-linear maps of $V$. For $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the square formed by $b_E$, $\operatorname{Res}b_\Omega$ and the canonical derived coefficient maps induced by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ commutes. The coefficient maps use the natural equality of invariants with scalar restriction. For $r=0$ the comparison is the identity $V_F[0]$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] with $R=C_F$, $J=L$, $H=D$, $u=\iota$. It constructs the specified canonical $b_F$, natural in equivariant maps, additive and compatible with shifts and connecting arrows. For fixed $F$, put $P(W)=$ "$b_F(W)$ is an isomorphism". Naturality makes $P$ invariant under equivariant isomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice analytic input; short assembly after Q62 re-split, step 1

proof.text: The trivial-representation case, including dimension zero, is [lem-sfb-trivial-dense-lattice-restriction]. If $T_i-1$ is invertible, it commutes with every action operator, so its inverse does too. Both are finite $E$-matrices and extend continuously over either $F$, giving inverse equivariant action-module maps. Apply [lem-sfb-central-action-derived-vanishing] to $z=\iota(e_i)$ in $L$ and $z=e_i$ in $D$. Both are central and act by $T_i$; both derived invariant objects vanish, so their comparison is invertible.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice analytic input; short assembly after Q62 re-split, step 2

proof.text: For every $L$-stable $U\subset W$, [lem-sfb-continuous-section-exact-triangles] supplies the short exact realization sequence and its comparison morphism of distinguished triangles. Shift compatibility from [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] verifies the remaining hypothesis of [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three]; hence $P(U)$ and $P(W/U)$ imply $P(W)$. Thus all three hypotheses of [lem-sfb-commuting-representation-devissage] hold, proving $P(V)$ for each $F$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice analytic input; short assembly after Q62 re-split, step 3

proof.text: For $H^0$, the calculus gives invariant inclusion. Integer representatives of residues modulo powers of $\ell$ show that $D$ is dense in $L$. If $m\in V_F(S)$ is fully $D$-fixed, each $m(s)$ is fixed by constant integers. The continuous function $x\mapsto x m(s)-m(s)$ has a closed zero set in $L$, since $F\otimes_E V$ is Hausdorff; density makes it zero everywhere. Hence after every $T\to S$, every continuous $g:T\to L$ fixes the pulled-back section pointwise. By [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] this is full $L$-invariance. The reverse inclusion is restriction, so $H^0(b_F)$ is the identity on the common submodule.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice analytic input; short assembly after Q62 re-split, step 4

proof.text: Naturality is that of the transformation in step 1. Let $\varphi:C_E\to C_\Omega$ be postcomposition by $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ and let $f:V_E\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi V_\Omega$ send $v$ to $1\otimes v$. It is continuous, equivariant and $C_E$-linear because both actions use the same $E$-matrices. The calculus's coefficient-pasting equality is precisely $c_D\circ b_E=(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi b_\Omega)\circ c_L$, with coefficient maps defined by $f$ and equality of invariants with scalar restriction. For $r=0$ both groups and $\iota$ are trivial; its normalization gives the identity on $V_F[0]$.
